title: From Prediction to Thinking: A Review of Reasoning in Industrial Recommender System
content: Thinking has become an increasingly visible theme in recommendation research, but the termcovers mechanisms with different purposes, computational costs, and evidential support. To ourknowledge, this work presents the first systematic review dedicated specifically to thinking andreasoning mechanisms in industrial recommender systems. We trace its development in orig-inal research involving major technology platforms, from behavioral prediction and semanticgrounding to explicit chain-of-thought, recommendation-specific post-training, latent reason-ing, and amortized reasoning services. We organize the literature along three complementaryaxes: what grounds an intermediate state, how that state is represented and consumed, andhow its usefulness is learned or verified. Twenty-five core reports involving Microsoft Research,Huawei, Shopee, Kuaishou, Tencent, Alibaba/Taobao, Meta, JD.com, Netflix, and Xiaohongshuare analyzed alongside historical foundations, search applications, and industrial alternatives.The evidence indicates that reasoning supervision, inference-time reasoning, and productionsystem improvements must be evaluated separately. Explicit thinking is not consistently supe-rior to direct prediction; compact or cached states can retain useful supervision while reducingserving cost; and reinforcement learning can optimize biased rewards as readily as useful recom-mendations. We distinguish company participation, proprietary-data evaluation, and random-ized online evidence, and propose an evaluation framework that combines predictive quality,intervention-based reasoning tests, serving eﬀiciency, and user utility. The resulting accounttreats thinking as a developing system capability whose value depends on grounding, feedback,and computation allocation.
